“I would first confirm the degree of anaemia and classify it according to MCV. I would take a focused history for dietary deficiency, blood loss, chronic disease, infection and haemoglobinopathy, and examine for pallor, jaundice and signs of cardiac compromise. Investigations would include FBC, blood film, ferritin and appropriate iron studies, with B12/folate, reticulocytes, haemoglobin electrophoresis and other tests guided by the findings. Iron deficiency would be treated with appropriate iron replacement and the underlying cause addressed. I would consider IV iron when oral therapy is unsuitable or rapid correction is required. In severe or symptomatic anaemia, I would assess urgently for haemodynamic or cardiac compromise and consider blood transfusion based on the clinical situation.”
